explainBack.question: If Chat and Cowork are now one conversation, why does Claude still sometimes stop and ask me before doing things, and why might a task die when I close my laptop?
explainBack.answer: The merge only removed the up-front choice of which mode to open; it did not remove the permission layer that governs actions. On the default Manual setting, Claude asks before each action and you approve or refuse it; switching that conversation to Auto reduces those check-ins. The setting applies to the whole conversation, so one choice governs all its actions. Separately, where the work runs determines survival: tasks touching files or apps on your computer need Claude Desktop open, so closing the laptop stops them, while tasks running in the cloud can keep going after the lid closes.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must use P005 (Manual asks before actions, Auto reduces check-ins, conversation-level scope), P007 (Desktop open for local work, cloud continues), and P004/P008 (doorway removed, decisions remain), without claiming the merge guarantees success or autonomy.
explainBack.assessment: The article fully supports this answer: every causal step comes from P004, P005, P007 and P008 with no gaps or invented material, so explain-back passes.

unseenTransfer.scenario: After the merge reaches her account, a freelancer asks Claude in one conversation to pull totals from twelve expense-receipt PDFs stored in a folder on her laptop and build a quarterly spreadsheet, then plans to close her laptop and catch a train while it finishes.
unseenTransfer.question: Using only the article's mechanism, what should she set and expect, and where will her plan break?
unseenTransfer.answer: She should keep the conversation on Manual so Claude asks before acting on each receipt file, name exactly which folder it may read, and verify every extracted amount against the original PDFs before trusting the spreadsheet. Her plan breaks at the train: because the receipts live on her laptop, this is local work that needs Claude Desktop open, so closing the lid stops it. Only cloud-run work continues after closure. She should either let the task finish before leaving or move the files to a cloud-accessible location first. Auto for the whole conversation would reduce check-ins but would apply to every action in it, so it is disproportionate for financial documents.
